cards.explanation: The answer is False. Joseph is a Council member, but Luke says he “…had not consented to their decision or action.” (Luke 23:51) He held a seat there without going along with them. I think that's a lonely spot to be in.

The answer is the body of Jesus. Joseph of Arimathea, the Council member, goes to Pilate, the governor, and asks for the body of Jesus. That's the whole request, plain and simple. Then Luke tells us what Joseph does next, and he does it with care. I think this was a man who knew exactly what he came for.

The answer is a tomb cut into the rock. Joseph wraps the body in linen and places it there. Luke tells us exactly where, so there's no guessing. The women from Galilee saw the tomb and how His body was placed (Luke 23:55). I think Joseph handled it with great care.
The answer is True. Luke says the tomb was one “…where no one had yet been laid.” (Luke 23:53) Nobody else had been placed in it before. Jesus is the first. I think that's worth noticing, friends.

The answer is the women from Galilee. Luke says the women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed. They saw the tomb and how His body was placed. They were there, and they saw it. I think they wanted to know where He was.

The answer is that they rest as the commandment says. Luke says they “…rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.” (Luke 23:56) The spices are ready, and they still wait. They don't rush the work. They rest first, and then they go back to the tomb.

The answer is the stone rolled away. The women find the stone rolled away from the tomb. They came with spices for a body, and what they find is an open tomb. I think that stopped them in their tracks. And Luke tells us it's only the beginning.

The answer is False. Luke says that when the women entered, “…they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.” (Luke 24:3) They came with spices, ready to care for Him. And they find the tomb without the body.

The answer is that they bow their faces to the ground. Luke says the women “…bowed their faces to the ground in terror…” (Luke 24:5) Two men in radiant apparel just appeared beside them. That's a lot for one morning. I'd be bowing too, friends.

The answer is He has risen. The two men say, “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6) That's the biggest news there is. The tomb is empty because Jesus is risen. They don't offer any other explanation.

The answer is third. Jesus said the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and “…on the third day rise again.” (Luke 24:7) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). He told them this ahead of time. And the two men tell the women to remember it.

The answer is the Eleven. The women report all these things to the Eleven and to all the others. Luke says the ones who told it were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and the other women with them. They told the apostles (Luke 24:10). I think they were eager to tell it.

The answer is False. Luke says, “But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.” (Luke 24:11) The women reported it, and to the apostles it seemed like nonsense. I think that was hard on the women.

The answer is that he runs to the tomb. Luke says Peter “…got up and ran to the tomb.” (Luke 24:12) Peter is one of the apostles, and the women's words had seemed like nonsense to them (Luke 24:11). But he doesn't sit still. He gets up and runs.

The answer is True. Luke says Peter, “…after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths…” went away. He looked in and saw the linen and nothing else. Then Luke says he went away wondering to himself what had happened. I think he had a lot to chew on, friends.
